newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tankan index positive for 1st time since Nov 91.
newsitem.headline: Tankan index positive for 1st time since Nov 91.

text.p: The diffusion index for big manufacturers turned positive for the first time since November 1991 in the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) "tankan" survey for March, a BOJ official said on Wednesday.
The index represents the percentage of firms expecting business conditions to improve minus those that expect them to worsen. The higher the number, the more optimistic the outlook.
In November 1991 the diffusion index for major manufacturers stood at plus 13.
The BOJ announced earlier on Wednesday that the index stood at plus 2 in its March 1997 survey, up from minus three in the previous survey in November.
The official said sentiment in the chemical and precision machinery sectors turned positive in the latest survey, and automobile manufacturers also showed a big improvement in sentiment.
Sales forecasts for big manufacturers increased for the fourth consecutive year, with the firms predicting sales growth of 2.6 percent in 1997/98.
Capital spending plans for all industries turned positive for the first time in five years, with an estimate of a 2.2 percent increase in 1996/97, the official said.
